title: Promote Yourself Without Promoting Yourself
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article addresses the tricky balance between self-promotion and being overlooked, arguing that overt self-promoters get labeled as having 'sharp elbows' while quiet, heads-down workers get taken for granted. It offers a practical workaround: leaders above you are always hungry for four types of information — updates on talented team members, major project or client news, market trends, and organizational blind spots — and feeding them these updates indirectly showcases your own results without ever saying 'I' or 'me.' A sample update is walked through to show how naming a teammate's win and a market insight simultaneously signals your own leadership and business acumen. The piece frames this as the 'secret' to self-promotion: communicate results through information your leaders already want, rather than direct credit-claiming.
points: Overt self-promotion earns distrust, while total silence about your work leads to being overlooked.
Leaders are hungry for four types of updates: team talent, big projects, market trends, and org blind spots.
Feeding leaders these four update types indirectly showcases your results without direct credit-claiming.
A sample update shows how naming a teammate's win can simultaneously signal your own leadership.
The core technique is to promote yourself by informing, not by claiming credit directly.
quotes: Leaders frown upon team members who hold themselves above the team, while colleagues distrust those who want to draw attention to themselves.
A failure to let those above know about the good work you’ve been doing is a recipe for being taken for granted.
For those frustrated by walking this tightrope, it’s time to learn the secret of self-promotion.
The more you update your leader on these four topics they always want to know, the more you indirectly promote yourself.
Those who aggressively self-promote their accomplishments are often viewed as having sharp elbows.
Leaders never forget those colleagues who skillfully walk the high wire of self-promotion.
